findings.text: The opening paragraph tells a newcomer what Athena is, who it is for and what problem it solves, in plain words. Someone who reads only this paragraph can say what the project is and why it matters.
findings.source: Athena is an open-source system, written in Rust, that turns a short request into a change to a code repository. ... It solves the problem of AI edits that arrive unreviewed and unaccountable.

findings.text: This is Athena's home page, but the title and heading are about a different project, firstmate. A newcomer who skims the title may think they landed on firstmate documentation and not on Athena's site.
findings.source: <title>Athena explains how firstmate handles work</title> / h1 "Athena explains how firstmate handles work"

findings.text: The first section after the intro is an error message. The lede promises a trace of models, cost and verdict, and this section was meant to show one but shows nothing. That hurts the page's case right where a newcomer is deciding whether to trust it.
findings.source: Check it on a real job: "The records of job 20261029-073603-7kqv could not be read here, so no models, verdict or costs are shown: no reading record for job 20261029-073603-7kqv."

findings.text: This link in the header is addressed to the owner, not a visitor. A newcomer cannot tell whether it applies to them, and it pulls attention from the next-step link next to it.
findings.source: "Owner view: proposals waiting for your decision."

findings.text: The next steps are concrete: prerequisites, a clone command, an install command and a first command to try. The header links straight to them, so a newcomer can find what to do next without reading the study.
findings.source: Next steps: "Before installing, have git 2.40 or later, a C linker, curl, and either Claude Code or npm" ... "./setup.sh" ... "athena ask \"add a changelog\""

findings.text: Almost all of the page is a detailed state-machine study of firstmate, down to exit codes 75 and 1 and lock behaviour. It is useful evidence of what Athena can produce, but it is far deeper than a newcomer to Athena needs. Apart from the intro and Next steps, the page does not say which parts a visitor can skip.
findings.source: Sections "Transitions", "Counters", "Why it is built this way" and "Claims and sources" (cards t1–t12, ra1–ra6, claims c1–c45)

findings.text: Several glossary entries say the term is undefined in the source. This is honest about the limits of the evidence, but it leaves the reader with words they still cannot interpret.
findings.source: Glossary: "The firstmate source does not define a durable record." / "The firstmate source does not define an endpoint." / "The firstmate source does not define a heartbeat."

findings.text: This refers to a repository folder that a newcomer has not seen and does not link to it. It does not help someone meeting the project for the first time.
findings.source: About this page: "This page's study id, firstmate-work-handling, is the name of the folder under studies/ that holds the data this page is generated from."

findings.text: The 'Start here' section is well organised: key terms first, then a step-by-step walk through one piece of work. A reader who wants to understand firstmate gets a clear way in.
findings.source: Start here: "The three parts below say what firstmate is, follow one piece of work, and say what happens when something fails or has no limit."
